"""A lowercase word/identifier beginning at a syntactic boundary.

The response is negative for content words after indentation, operators,
argument delimiters, type names, and code keywords. Whitespace-prefixed,
longer word pieces respond more than attached fragments. English function
words and structural code keywords damp the response. Capitalized
words after indentation have a weaker negative response. Ordinary word
continuations, numbers, and non-Latin text stay near zero.

Two previous tokens supply the boundary; document changes clear them.
The numbers are coarse strengths fitted on training text, not token IDs.
"""
READS = ()

FUNCTION_WORDS = set('''
a an the this that these those i you he she it we they me him her us them
my your his its our their who whom whose which what where when why how
and or but nor yet so if then else than as of to in on at by for from with
without about into onto upon under over through during before after between
against among within out up down off not no yes is am are was were be being
been has have had do does did will would shall should may might can could
must also both each either neither every all any some such many much more
most less least few other another same only very too just even still already
however therefore
'''.split())

STRUCTURAL_KEYWORDS = set('''
return const let var def class function public private protected static final
async await export import package namespace using interface extends implements
abstract switch case break continue while for if else try catch finally throw
throws yield lambda elif elseif foreach declare echo pass end pub fn mut
assert raise del with
'''.split())
BUILTINS_AND_LITERALS = set('''
void int float double char long short byte boolean bool string str object new
delete typeof instanceof null nil true false None True False self super print
'''.split())
TYPE_NAMES = set('''
String Integer Object List Map Set File Path Date DateTime Number Boolean Byte
Double Float Long Short Character Throwable Exception Type T
'''.split())
INTRODUCERS = set('''
return const let var def class function public private protected static final
async await export import package namespace using void int float double char
long short byte boolean bool string str object new for if else elif foreach
assert print pub fn mut from del raise param define
'''.split())


def boundary_strength(token, previous, prior):
    """Strength of the boundary before the current word piece."""
    word = previous.strip()
    end = previous.rstrip()[-1:]
    indent = len(previous) - len(previous.rstrip(' \t'))
    if not previous.isspace():
        indent = 0
    indent += len(token) - len(token.lstrip('\t'))
    if not previous or previous.startswith('<|'):
        return 0.0
    if indent:
        return 1.0 if indent >= 3 else 0.76
    if previous.isspace():
        return 0.66
    if end.isascii() and end.isalpha():
        if word in TYPE_NAMES:
            return 0.53
        if word in INTRODUCERS:
            if prior.isspace() and prior.strip('\r\n'):
                return 0.83
            return 0.10 if previous[:1].isspace() else 0.53
        return 0.0
    if end.isdigit():
        return 0.10
    if end == ':':
        return 0.57
    if end in '=+-*/%<>|&':
        return 0.68 if previous[:1].isspace() else 0.39
    if end in '\'"`':
        return 0.50
    if end in '([{':
        return 0.77 if previous[:1].isspace() else 0.84
    if end in ',;':
        return 0.36 if previous[:1].isspace() else 0.20
    if end == '.':
        return 0.41
    return 0.24 if len(word) < 8 else 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous = prior = ''
    else:
        _, previous, prior = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    state = (doc, token, previous)
    word = token.lstrip()
    first = word[:1]
    if not first or not first.isascii() or not first.islower():
        indent = len(previous) - len(previous.rstrip(' \t'))
        if first.isascii() and first.isupper() and previous.isspace():
            return state, -0.15 if indent >= 3 else 0.007
        return state, 0.007

    # Each pair is (attached fragment, whitespace-prefixed word piece).
    leading = int(token[:1].isspace())
    length = min(len(word), 4) - 1
    if word in STRUCTURAL_KEYWORDS:
        strength = ((0.0, 0.13, 0.06, 0.06),
                    (0.0, 0.09, -0.32, -0.22))[leading][length]
    elif word in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        strength = ((0.13, -0.02, -0.05, -0.12),
                    (-0.15, -0.27, -0.20, -0.48))[leading][length]
    elif word in BUILTINS_AND_LITERALS:
        strength = -0.71 if leading else -0.40
    else:
        strength = ((0.09, -0.11, -0.31, -0.51),
                    (-0.45, -0.98, -1.17, -1.35))[leading][length]
    return state, float(strength * boundary_strength(token, previous, prior))

"""Layer 0, MLP output channel 256: a "bare name" detector.

The component goes negative on a plain lowercase word that stands alone as a
name: a variable, field, object or type name in source code (result, name,
instance, country, margin), or a label in a list or table. It is strongest when
the word starts a line or follows indentation (-1.1), weaker after an operator or
bracket (-0.8), after a language keyword (-0.2), or right after a bracket or dot
with no space (-0.25). In running prose the same slots give about half as much.
Grammar words, keywords used as keywords, capitalised words, numbers and
punctuation stay near zero, and so does a word that follows another ordinary
word, as in a sentence.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# English function words and programming keywords: never read as a name here.
FUNCTION_WORDS = set(
    """a an the of to in on at for from by with and or but if then else so as is are
    was were be been being it its this that these those there here he she they we you
    i me my your our their his her them us not no do does did have has had will would
    can could should may might must shall just also than too very about into over
    under up down out off again once what which who whom whose when where why how all
    any both each few more most other some such only own same
    elif while return def class import public private protected static void var let
    const int char float double bool boolean fn func struct case break continue
    try catch throw throws except finally switch default extends implements
    yield async await use using package include require export""".split()
)
# Characters that mark code rather than prose.
CODE_CHARS = set("{}()[];=<>+*/&|!$%#\\:")
# Mean activation per (slot, setting), fitted on training rows.
VALUES = {
    ("blank", "code"): -1.1,
    ("blank", "prose"): -0.67,
    ("punct_sp", "code"): -0.8,
    ("punct_sp", "prose"): -0.25,
    ("punct_tight", "code"): -0.25,
    ("punct_tight", "prose"): -0.16,
    ("kw", "code"): -0.19,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    name = token.strip()
    if not (name.isalpha() and name.islower() and len(name) > 1) or name in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return carry, 0.0
    if len(prefix.token_strings) < 2:
        return carry, 0.0
    # Code or prose: share of code characters in the last 40 tokens.
    recent = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-41:-1])
    code = sum(ch in CODE_CHARS for ch in recent) / max(1, len(recent))
    where = "code" if code >= 0.05 else "prose"
    # The slot: what comes just before the word.
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    if before == "" or token.startswith("\t"):
        slot = "blank"
    elif before in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        slot = "kw"
    elif not before[-1].isalnum():
        slot = "punct_sp" if token.startswith(" ") else "punct_tight"
    else:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, VALUES.get((slot, where), 0.0)

"""Use nearby code and path punctuation as a shrunken activation cue."""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        recent = ""
    else:
        recent = carry[1]
    recent = (recent + token)[-120:]

    marks = ("{", "}", ";", "=>", "->", "::", "</", "_", "==", "/")
    code = any(mark in recent for mark in marks)
    word = token.lstrip()
    if word and word[0].isalpha():
        raw = -0.75 if code else (-0.18 if token != word else 0.0)
    else:
        raw = 0.0
    return (doc, recent), 0.14 * raw + 0.007

"""Future-tense / modal auxiliary detector for one MLP neuron of layer 0.

The neuron fires on the word that introduces a future or modal verb phrase, so the
next token is a bare verb: " will" ("you WILL see"), "'ll" ("I'LL check"), " would",
" might", " shall", " may", and the "going" + "to" of "is GOING TO be" (the "to" is
the strongest). "won't" fires on the "'t" after "won" but not on "don't" or "can't".
The future markers 会 and 将 in Chinese and werden/wird in German also fire.
Words that do not mark the future (should, can, must, need, have to, is) stay near 0.
Every other token is predicted as 0.
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS = ()

# Typical activation on each auxiliary, measured on training text
FUTURE_AUX = {
    " will": 5.2, " Will": 4.1, "Will": 4.7, "will": 4.1,
    "'ll": 3.4, "’ll": 4.1,
    " would": 1.2, " might": 0.9, " shall": 0.9, " may": 0.7,
    " going": 0.9, " werden": 1.0, " wird": 0.8,
    "会": 2.5, "将": 0.9,
}
NEGATION_CLITICS = {"'t", "’t"}   # "won't": the "'t" after " won" only
GOING_TO = 2.3                    # the " to" in "going to"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    if token in NEGATION_CLITICS:
        return None, (5.5 if previous.strip() == "won" else 0.0)
    if token == " to" and previous == " going":
        return None, GOING_TO
    return None, FUTURE_AUX.get(token, 0.0)

"""Fires negatively on words for tags, labels, signatures and signing, and more weakly on
other words for marking or fastening things (stamps, seals, tape, ties, sticking).

The program is a word lookup: each token, lower-cased and stripped of punctuation such as
'_', '.', '(' or '/', is looked up in three tiers of meaning. The predicted activation is
the tier's typical value; every other token gives 0.
"""

READS = ()

# Strongest: tags and signatures, English and Chinese (签 = sign, 标签 = label).
TAG_SIGNATURE = {
    "tag", "tags", "tagged", "tagging", "tagname",
    "signature", "signatures", "签", "签名", "签字", "签署", "签订", "标签",
}
# Middle: labels and the verb 'to sign'.
LABEL_SIGN = {
    "label", "labels", "labeled", "labelled", "labeling",
    "signed", "signing",
    "atures",  # the tail of 'Signatures' when split as 'Sign' + 'atures'
}
# Weak: other words for marking or fastening things.
MARKING = {
    "sign", "signs", "sig", "unsigned", "stamp", "seal", "stuck", "stickers", "tape",
    "tie", "ties", "tied", "tight", "tab", "tabs", "stencil", "tattoo", "badge",
    "票", "牌", "封", "标记",
}

STRONG_VALUE = -3.0
MIDDLE_VALUE = -1.2
WEAK_VALUE = -0.5


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().strip("_./()\"' ").lower()
    if word in TAG_SIGNATURE:
        return None, STRONG_VALUE
    if word in LABEL_SIGN:
        return None, MIDDLE_VALUE
    if word in MARKING:
        return None, WEAK_VALUE
    return None, 0.0

"""Approximate a local person-and-attribute relationship.

After named human nouns or pronouns, possession, having, 'with' and
relative-clause links are negative; 'and/or' coordination is positive.
Basic/family nouns are weaker than occupational roles. Animal/group nouns
and association words have weaker related responses. Recognized Chinese
and Japanese markers follow the same idea. A six-token supplying-verb
memory strengthens 'with'. The separate /usr/local spelling pattern is
positive. Other positions predict zero; document boundaries reset memory.
"""
READS = ()

HUMAN_NOUNS = frozenset('''person persons people individual human man men woman
women boy girl child children kid adult infant teenager baby male female
student patient resident citizen user customer consumer client worker employee
farmer scientist researcher author writer reader artist actor singer photographer

suspect stranger alien character bachelor entrepreneur friend neighbor mother

audience population congregation crowd inhabitant supporter follower volunteer

neighbor mother father parent son daughter brother sister husband wife relative
family king queen'''.split())
EXPLICIT_PEOPLE = frozenset('''someone somebody anyone anybody everyone everybody
nobody people person persons individual individuals'''.split())
SUBJECTS = frozenset('he she they we i'.split())
OBJECTS = frozenset('''you me him her us them myself yourself yourselves themselves
himself herself oneself'''.split())
ANIMALS_AND_GROUPS = frozenset('''animal dog cat bird creature horse bee insect fish
company organization team government party country tribe'''.split())
SUPPLYING = frozenset('''provide provides provided providing equip equipping
supply supplies supplying give gives giving furnish furnishing instill instilling
challenge'''.split())
EQUIPPED = frozenset('''provided equipped armed identified diagnosed born present
presenting presented'''.split())
ASSOCIATED = frozenset('associated consistent familiar treated'.split())
CJK_PEOPLE = frozenset('''人 人民 人们 人們 大家 众 眾 居民 市民 学生 學生
大学生 大學生 女孩 男孩 女人 男人 女子 男子 儿童 兒童 孩子 家长 家長
家人 朋友 伙伴 夥伴 小伙伴 老师 老師 教师 教師 医生 醫生 患者 病人
客人 客户 客戶 用户 用戶 玩家 粉丝 粉絲 职工 職工 员工 員工 工人
司机 司機 同志 选手 選手 青年 人物 民众 民眾 大众 大眾 公众 公眾
你 他 她 我 我们 我們 他们 他們 您 你们 你們 同学 同學 他人 友人'''.split())

# Nominal relationships; constants are activation estimates, not probabilities.
LINK = {
    "'s": -0.86, 'with': -1.82, 'and': 0.45, 'or': 0.34,
    'have': -0.76, 'has': -0.75, 'having': -0.85, 'had': -0.43,
    'who': -0.28, 'that': -0.70, 'whose': -0.71, 'of': -0.06,
    'without': -0.61,
}


def person_strength(word):
    singular = word[:-3] + 'y' if word.endswith('ies') else word.rstrip('s')
    if word in EXPLICIT_PEOPLE:
        return 1.12
    if word in FAMILY_AND_BASIC_PEOPLE or singular in FAMILY_AND_BASIC_PEOPLE:
        return 0.78
    if word in OBJECTS:
        return 0.55
    if word in HUMAN_NOUNS or singular in HUMAN_NOUNS:
        return 1.0
    if word in ('who', 'those', 'others', 'each', 'one', 'else', 'many'):
        return 0.45
    if word in ANIMALS_AND_GROUPS or singular in ANIMALS_AND_GROUPS:
        return 0.30
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = int(prefix.document_ids[-1])
    previous, giving = carry[1:] if carry and carry[0] == doc else ('', 0)
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    relation = "'s" if token in ("'s", '’s', "'", '’') else word
    strength = person_strength(previous)
    value = strength * LINK.get(relation, 0.0)
    if relation in ('and', 'or') and strength:
        value /= strength ** 0.5
    if relation == 'of' and previous in EXPLICIT_PEOPLE:
        value = -0.54
    if previous in SUBJECTS:
        value = {"'s": -0.21, 'and': 0.15, 'has': -0.23, 'have': -0.07,
                 'had': -0.06}.get(relation, 0.0)
        if previous == 'they' and relation == 'have':
            value = -0.27
    elif previous in OBJECTS:
        value = {'with': -0.90 if previous == 'you' else -0.60,
                 'and': 0.24, 'or': 0.14, 'have': -0.14, 'that': -0.27,
                 'had': -0.07
                 }.get(relation, 0.0)
    if previous == 'those' and relation == 'with':
        value = -1.45
    if previous == 'who' and relation in ('has', 'have'):
        value = -0.45
    cjk = previous in CJK_PEOPLE or previous.endswith(
        ('人员', '人員', '工作者', '参与者', '參與者', '表演者',
         '设计师', '設計師', '创始人', '創始人'))
    if cjk:
        value = {'的': -0.90, '有': -0.90, 'の': -0.65, '和': 0.45,
                 '与': 0.45, '與': 0.45, '及': 0.60, '是': -0.25
                 }.get(token, value)
    if token in ('人的', '人都', '人均', '们', '們'):
        value -= 0.50
    if relation == 'with':
        if previous in EQUIPPED:
            value = -0.85
        elif previous in ASSOCIATED:
            value = -0.23
        elif giving and strength:
            value -= 1.0 if previous in OBJECTS else 0.75
    if previous.endswith('usr') and token == '/local':
        value = 1.37
    giving = 6 if word in SUPPLYING else max(0, giving - 1)
    return (doc, word, giving), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:259: a "person-context" detector on the token after a people word.

What it does, in plain terms:
- It is mostly quiet. Its large responses come when the token right before is a word for a
  person or group of people (people, users, patients, students, mother, who, they, you, me,
  ...), and the current token is a word that attaches something to that person:
    * "with" after a people word is strongly negative ("patients with", "users with",
      "provide me with"): about -1.6.
    * "'s" / "’s" / "的" (possessive) after a people word: about -0.7 to -1.4.
    * "that", "has", "who", "which", "whose", "have": mildly to moderately negative.
    * "and" / "or" after a people word are mildly positive (a coordinated list of people).
- Verbs that give something to a person ("provided with", "equipped with", "diagnosed with")
  also make "with" negative, less strongly.
- "with" elsewhere is slightly negative; "with" in fixed phrases ("in connection with",
  "in accordance with") is slightly positive.
- Everything else is predicted as 0. The component's many small, token-specific values
  elsewhere are not modelled here.

Weights are rough means read off a sample of training rows (activation units).
"""

READS = ()

# Words for people or groups of people, pronouns for them, and a few Chinese people nouns.
PEOPLE = set("""
user users people person persons men man woman women child children kid kids
patient patients customer customers student students employee employees worker workers
veteran veterans mother mothers father fathers parent parents individual individuals
someone anyone everyone guy citizen citizens resident residents taxpayer taxpayers
athlete athletes player players actor actors scientist scientists member members
traveler travelers vendor vendors entrepreneur manufacturer audience audiences family
friend friends boy girl son daughter wife husband teacher doctor lawyer consumer buyer
seller viewer farmer scholar subjects animals
me us him her them you he she they we who whom those
人 人民 居民 村民 员工 职工 玩家 学生 患者 病人 用户 客户 顾客 男性 女性 儿童 人员
观众 人们 他们 我们
""".split())

# Verbs that give something to a person; "with" after them attaches a thing to the person.
GIVING_VERBS = set("""
provide provides provided providing equip equipped equips supply supplied
diagnosed infected identified armed
""".split())

# Fixed phrases where "with" is not about a person: slightly positive.
FIXED_WITH = set("connection accordance agreement completed keeping stuck balance relationship".split())

# Activation after a people word, for the current token (other tokens: 0).
AFTER_PEOPLE = {
    "with": -1.6, "'s": -0.75, "’s": -0.7, "的": -1.4, "'": -0.4, "that": -0.5,
    "has": -0.45, "who": -0.3, "whose": -0.8, "which": -0.5, "have": -0.17,
    "and": 0.4, "or": 0.3,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token, from the token before it (zero at a document start)."""
    if len(prefix) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return None, 0.0
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    if cur == "with":
        if prev in PEOPLE:
            return None, -1.6
        if prev in GIVING_VERBS:
            return None, -0.9
        if prev in FIXED_WITH:
            return None, 0.3
        return None, -0.1
    if prev in PEOPLE:
        return None, float(AFTER_PEOPLE.get(cur, 0.0))
    return None, 0.0

"""A sparse, word-level proxy for possessive and association cues.

It predicts negative values at genitive markers, “have/has,” and a few
related words; it leaves other positions at zero. This is only a small
heuristic for the component's context-dependent activations.
"""
READS = ()

PRONOUNS = frozenset({
    "i", "me", "my", "we", "us", "our", "you", "your",
    "he", "him", "his", "she", "her", "it", "its",
    "they", "them", "their", "who", "that", "there",
})


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    previous = ""
    if (len(prefix) > 1
            and prefix.document_ids[-1] == prefix.document_ids[-2]):
        previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()

    if word in ("'s", "’s"):
        if previous.isalpha() and previous.lower() not in PRONOUNS:
            return None, -0.16
        return None, 0.0
    if word in ("'", "’"):
        if previous.isalpha() and previous.lower().endswith("s"):
            return None, -0.18
        return None, -0.04
    if word == "的":
        return None, -0.03
    if word.lower() in ("has", "have"):
        return None, -0.12
    if (word.lower() == "with" and not word[:1].isupper()
            and previous.isalpha()):
        return None, -0.04
    return None, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""Approximate a mathematical-notation versus code/currency response.

Count recognizable math, programming, and money cues in the last 1000
characters. Use this evidence to give formula-introducing dollars a negative
value and programming/currency dollars a positive one. Token spacing and
punctuation distinguish likely introductions from closing marks. Smaller
rules cover backticks, thinking tags, formal setup words, sterling, and TeX's
opening parenthesis. All remaining tokens get zero. Reset at each document.
"""
import math
import re

READS = ()
MATH_WORDS = set('''equation equations formula formulas theorem lemma proof
vector vectors matrix matrices scalar polynomial integer integers coefficient
coefficients probability derivative integral algebra quantum hamiltonian
eigenvalue eigenvalues subspace momentum tensor tensors permutation triangle
radius velocity acceleration reciprocal sum product sequence sqrt sin cos log
divisor factors eigenvectors curvature subinterval nondegenerate homomorphism
asymptote genotype parameter parameters variable variables function functions
set sets limit solution solutions denote denotes denoted'''.split())
MONEY_WORDS = set('''cost costs price prices pay paid dollars cash million billion
funds income earnings worth valued deposit refund refundable budget capital
expensive cheap stock shares money financial currency fee fees'''.split())
CODE_WORDS = set('''public private protected foreach echo const async import
export return class def function environment shell bash php javascript rust
git python string boolean null int'''.split())
SETUP_WORDS = MATH_WORDS | {
    'given', 'let', 'suppose', 'assume', 'definition', 'numbers', 'number', 'real'}
GREEK_MATH = set('αβγδεθλμνξπρσφψωΓΔΘΛΞΠΣΦΨΩ')
LATEX = re.compile(
    r'\\(?:frac|dfrac|sqrt|sum|int|lim|in|math\w*|alpha|beta|gamma|delta|'
    r'lambda|theta|sigma|phi|psi|omega|begin|end|rightarrow|overline|pm|hat|'
    r'ce|to|colon|times|pi|rangle|langle|text\w*|displaystyle|sim|cdot|geq|leq|'
    r'partial|nabla|ell|vec|big|left|right|ldots|cdots|ref|eqref|label)\b')


def context(text):
    """Graded evidence of mathematics, source code, and financial prose."""
    words = re.findall(r'[a-z]+', text.lower())
    latex = min(len(LATEX.findall(text)) / 3, 1)
    formulas = min(len(re.findall(r'\$[A-Za-z](?![A-Za-z])', text)) / 3, 1)
    math_count = sum(w in MATH_WORDS for w in words)
    math_words = min(math_count / 5, 1)

  "such", "look", "need", "going", "used", "due"), it is weaker, and for "in" and
  "to" almost off ("involved in", "going to", "need to");

"""Recognize distinctive Go code: its file names and declaration syntax.

Go's short declarations, function headers, slices, and exported calls are
the main cues. Nearby Go code also makes its common types and control words
slightly positive; the program does not try to interpret code generally.
"""

import re

READS = ()

_GO_FILE = re.compile(r"\.go$")
_FUNC = re.compile(r"\bfunc\s*$")
_WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_]+$")
_GO_HINT = re.compile(
    r":=|\[\]|\.go\b|\.New\b|\.With\b|"
    r"^\s*package\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*$"
)
_GO_WORDS = {
    "bool": 1.2, "chan": 1.5, "err": 1.3, "map": 0.8,
    "nil": 1.4, "return": 1.2, "string": 1.0, "struct": 0.8,
    "type": 0.6, "var": 0.4,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc, history = carry if carry is not None else (None, "")
    current_doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc != current_doc:
        history = ""
    text = (history + prefix.token_strings[-1])[-240:]
    ending = text.rstrip()

    score = 0.0
    if _GO_FILE.search(ending):
        score += 4.0
    if ending.endswith("golang"):
        score += 3.0
    if ending.endswith(":="):
        score += 2.5
    if _FUNC.search(ending):
        before = ending[:-4].lower()
        score += 1.0 if before.endswith(("public ", "override ")) else 4.5
    if ending.endswith("[]"):
        score += 1.8

    method = re.search(r"\.([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)$", ending)
    if method:
        name = method.group(1)
        score += 4.0 if name == "New" else 2.3 if name == "With" else 0.7

    go_context = bool(_GO_HINT.search(text))
    if go_context:
        word = _WORD.findall(ending)
        if word:
            score += _GO_WORDS.get(word[-1], 0.0)

    return (current_doc, text), score

in prose-like context. Percent signs also strengthen after numbers. A rolling
count of space-prefixed alphabetic tokens estimates prose context. Whitespace

hyphens, minus signs and selected document-initial symbols have negative rules.

unexplained. Coefficients were fitted on training text, not a vocabulary table.

# following-whitespace correction, leading-space correction.
SYMBOLS = {
    '%': (0.25, 0.28, 0.26, 0.00, -0.12),
    ']': (0.14, 0.34, -0.09, 0.00, 0.00),
    '&': (0.15, 0.40, -0.04, -0.03, 0.00),
    '/': (0.01, 0.41, -0.03, 0.16, 0.05),
    '+': (0.05, 0.43, -0.07, 0.00, -0.02),
    '=': (-0.01, 0.12, -0.04, 0.00, 0.02),
    '|': (-0.04, 0.25, -0.13, -0.07, 0.07),
    '@': (0.10, 0.34, 0.00, 0.00, -0.12),
    '-': (0.02, -0.12, 0.00, 0.00, 0.02),
}
UNITS = {'s', 'sec', 'min', 'h', 'hr', 'm', 'cm', 'mm', 'kg', 'day', 'year'}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, word_flags, word_count = '', (), 0
    else:
        _, previous, word_flags, word_count = carry

    symbol = token.strip()
    preceding = previous.strip()
    prose = min(word_count / 8.0, 1.0)
    lexical = (float(preceding.isalpha()) * min(len(preceding) / 3.0, 1.0)
               * (0.15 + 0.85 * prose))
    number = float(preceding.isdigit())
    whitespace = float(previous.isspace())
    leading = float(token.startswith(' '))

    # A symbol fused to a sentence-ending comma/period has a weaker response.
    scale = 1.0
    if symbol in {'%.', '%,', '].', '],'}:
        symbol = symbol[0]
        scale = 0.45

    if symbol in SYMBOLS:
        base, word, digit, blank, space = SYMBOLS[symbol]
        value = (base + word * lexical + digit * number
                 + blank * whitespace + space * leading) * scale
    elif symbol == '[':
        value = (0.05 + 0.09 * leading + 0.46 * leading * lexical
                 - 0.04 * float('\n' in previous))
    elif symbol == '\\':
        value = 0.01 + 0.39 * leading * lexical - 0.06 * number
    elif symbol == '>':
        value = (-0.03 + 0.38 * leading * lexical
                 + 0.08 * leading + 0.06 * whitespace)
    elif symbol == '<':
        value = 0.23 * leading * lexical - 0.06 * number
    elif token.startswith('/') and token[1:].isalpha():
        value = -0.01 + 0.38 * lexical
        # The disjunction in "and/or".
        if token == '/or' and preceding.lower() == 'and':
            value += 0.54
        elif token[1:] in UNITS:
            value += 0.12
    elif token == '    ':
        value = 0.08 - 0.10 * number + whitespace * (0.03 + 0.33 * prose)
    elif token == '\t':
        value = 0.02 - 0.05 * number + 0.03 * whitespace * prose
    elif token == ' \n\n':
        value = -0.67 if not previous else 0.02 - 0.06 * lexical
    elif symbol == '\u00ad':
        value = -0.45
    elif symbol == '\u2212':
        value = -0.12
    else:
        value = 0.0

    if not previous and symbol in {'/', '-'}:
        value = -0.23 if symbol == '/' else -0.20

    is_word = int(token.startswith(' ') and symbol.isalpha() and len(symbol) > 1)
    if len(word_flags) == 16:
        word_count -= word_flags[0]
        word_flags = word_flags[1:]
    word_flags += (is_word,)
    word_count += is_word
    return (doc, token, word_flags, word_count), float(value)

residual stream. It is switched on by

  * the digit 8 (about 0.66 inside a number, 0.52 otherwise),
  * a "0" that comes straight after a "2", i.e. the "0" of "20xx" years (about 1.0),

value. Word endings of English place names (-boro, -ville, -hurst, -brook) and Chinese
administrative suffixes (县 county, 市 city, 镇 town, 陵, 山) count too.

    "Falls": 1.5, "Ridge": 1.5, "Moines": 2.0, "Verde": 2.0, "Dale": 1.5,

    "Tech": 1.0, "Institute": 1.0, "Award": 0.8, "League": 0.8, "Festival": 0.8,
    "Society": 0.8, "Library": 0.6, "School": 0.7, "Hall": 0.7, "Ltd": 0.8, "News": 0.8,
    "Press": 0.9, "Airport": 0.9, "Station": 0.8, "Bridge": 0.7, "State": 0.7,

    "brook": 2.0, "ford": 1.5, "field": 1.2, "wood": 1.0, "burg": 1.2, "bury": 1.2,
}

    word = ""

concepts, fields, institutions and processes: "technologies", "theories", "economies",

("members", "jerseys") stay near zero.

  - a suffix piece (no leading space) or a whole word (leading space);
  - its plural ending: "-ies" strongest, then the abstract Latinate endings, then
    "-ses" and "-es".

PERSON_ENDINGS = ("ers", "ors", "ists", "ians", "men")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip()
    piece = not tok.startswith(" ")  # no leading space: a suffix piece of a longer word

    if word.endswith("ses"):  # analyses, databases
        return None, 0.20

    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection component 287: a "minimum / administrative" word detector.

The component reads the current token only (no context needed). It writes a large
activation on tokens that spell words of the "minimum" family, the "administrative"
family, or "maximum"/"least"-type words, and is near zero on almost everything else.

Each token is scored by the word it spells (lowercased, leading punctuation and spaces
dropped):
  * core "minimum" sense: "min", "minimum", "minimal", "minimize", "minim..." (also
    " min", "=min", "/min", "MIN", "Min") -> about 4.5.
  * other words starting with "min": mining, mine, minister, minute, minor, minus,
    minority, mini, Minnesota -> about 2.2. The words "mind", "minded", "ming", "mint"
    are not this family and get 0.
  * contains "admin" (administrative, administration, Admin) -> about 2.6.
  * Chinese 矿 (mine) and 行政 (administrative) -> about 3.0.
  * starts with "max" (maximum, max, Max) -> about 1.2.
  * "least" or "smallest" -> about 1.4.
  * anything else -> 0.

Values are the least-squares fit on 600 training rows (variance explained about 0.65).
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Words starting with "min" that are not the "minimum" sense: mind, minded, ming, mint.
NOT_MIN = re.compile(r"min(d|g|t)")


def concept_value(token: str) -> float:
    text = token.strip()
    word = re.sub(r"^[^a-z]*", "", text.lower())
    if text in ("矿", "行政"):
        return 3.0
    if word.startswith("min") and not NOT_MIN.match(word):
        if word == "min" or word.startswith("minim"):
            return 4.5
        return 2.2
    if "admin" in word:
        return 2.6
    if word.startswith("max"):
        return 1.2
    if word in ("least", "smallest"):
        return 1.4
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # Each position depends only on its own token, so the carry is unused.
    return carry, float(concept_value(prefix.token_strings[-1]))

"""Apostrophe and single-quote detector (layer 0, MLP unit 312, down_proj).

The unit is quiet on almost every token. It goes clearly negative on the
single-quote characters themselves: the straight apostrophe ' and the curly
quotes ‘ ’ (and similar marks), as they appear in the token. Its size depends
on what the quote is attached to:

- a lone quote, one that opens a quoted string or stands alone ( ' , " ('", " '",
  "['", "‘" ): about -2.3;
- a quote that ends a word or a quoted string, followed by a suffix or
  punctuation ('s, 're, 'll, 'm, ',  ';  ':  ')  ): about -1.1;
- the t of n't ('t, ’t): slightly positive, +0.2.

Backticks and quote-free tokens are 0. Nothing depends on earlier tokens.

APOSTROPHES = "'‘’ʻ′"  # ' ‘ ’ ʻ ′
OPENERS = " ([{\"`"  # what may sit in front of an opening quote
ENDINGS = ",;:)]}.!?\n "  # what may follow a closing quote


def quote_activation(token: str) -> float:
    """The unit's activation on one token, from the quote characters it holds."""
    index = next((i for i, ch in enumerate(token) if ch in APOSTROPHES), None)
    if index is None:
        return 0.0
    before, after = token[:index], token[index + 1 :]
    if after == "t":
        return 0.2
    if after.isalpha() or (after and all(ch in ENDINGS for ch in after)):
        if before.strip(OPENERS) == "":
            return -1.1
    return -2.3

    """Called once per token; the carry is unused because the rule is local."""
    return None, quote_activation(prefix.token_strings[-1])

into the residual stream. Its activation depends on which token is being read, not on
context: it is near zero for ordinary common words, punctuation and code symbols (low

tokens at the top of the vocabulary (ids >= 151643: <|endoftext|>, chat and tool

"""Layer 0, MLP down_proj component 317: a word-split detector.

It is silent on almost every token. It fires when the current token completes a word that the
previous token started, and only for particular pairs of pieces:
- 'bed' after a piece ending in 'test' (testbed, as in '/testbed/...'): about +1.6.
- a few other pairs whose join is a known word or name, e.g. 'Viet|nam', 'pot|ter', 'Pent|house':
  about +1.6.
- a few pairs with a negative response, e.g. 'et|ilde', 'ot|iv' (Cyrillic 'от|ив'): about -0.8.
Everything else predicts 0. Pairs are matched exactly on the two pieces as the tokenizer splits
them, with a leading space or slash ignored.
"""

POSITIVE = {
    ("Viet", "nam"), ("pot", "ter"), ("crit", "ter"), ("Pent", "house"), ("Put", "nam"),
    ("met", "form"), ("St", "j"), ("ST", "K"), ("t", "zip"), ("IT", "s"), ("Kat", "sum"),
}
NEGATIVE = {("et", "ilde"), ("ot", "iv"), ("от", "ив"), ("ат", "ив")}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if len(prefix) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lstrip("/")
    if cur == "bed" and prev.endswith("test"):
        return carry, 1.6
    if (prev, cur) in POSITIVE:
        return carry, 1.6
    if (prev, cur) in NEGATIVE:
        return carry, -0.8
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:318: a negation-contraction and code-opener detector.

This component is almost silent. Its large responses are concentrated on a few concepts,
and most of its variance is a diffuse, token-specific background that this program does
not capture. What the program does:

1. Negative contraction suffix. The token "'t" (or the typographic "’t") written after a
   word, as in can't, doesn't, won't, didn't. It responds most to "can't" (about 0.55 on
   the suffix) and about 0.3 to the other negative contractions.
2. "cannot" responds weakly (about 0.19). "not" right after do/does/did responds weakly
   (about 0.1).
3. Document openers. Where a new document starts (the document id changes, which is just
   after <|endoftext|>), a first token that opens a code file or a markup/heading block
   ("#", "##", "#include", "package", "using", "import", "<?", "//", "/*", "#!/") gives a
   strong response (about 0.7). The same tokens mid-document give almost nothing.

Every other token predicts 0. Values are the rounded means measured on training rows.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Suffixes of a negative contraction: can't, don't, won't ...
NEGATION_SUFFIX = {"'t", "’t"}
# Words that come right before the suffix in can't.
CAN = {" can", "Can", "can"}
# Auxiliaries before "not" in do not / does not / did not.
DO = {" do", " does", " did", "Do", "Does", "Did"}
# First tokens of a document that open code or a markup/heading block.
CODE_OPENERS = {"#", "##", "#include", "package", "using", "import", "<?", "//", "/*", "#!/"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    doc = prefix.document_ids
    starts_document = len(doc) == 1 or doc[-1] != doc[-2]

    if starts_document and tok in CODE_OPENERS:
        return carry, 0.7
    if tok in NEGATION_SUFFIX:
        return carry, 0.55 if before in CAN else 0.3
    if tok == " cannot":
        return carry, 0.19
    if tok == " not" and before in DO:
        return carry, 0.1
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:319 -- a weak, mostly diffuse feature with a few sharp triggers.

What it does, in plain terms:
  * Most of the time it is near zero, with small wiggles that depend on which word is
    present; no simple word class captures those wiggles, so this program leaves them at 0.
  * It fires most strongly on the word right after a copula ("is" / "was") when that word
    opens a restatement or purpose clause: "That is[,] ...", "the task is [to] ...",
    "the purpose was [to] ...", "This is [it] ...", "is [in/on/at/then] ...".
  * It also fires on "with" in "has to do with" and on a document-initial " for".
  * It is pushed negative on " to" in "due to".

The program predicts these triggers as the typical activation seen in training data.

# Typical activation of the word that directly follows a copula.
AFTER_COPULA = {
    ",": 0.38,      # "That is, ..." / "The reality is, ..."
    " to": 0.22,    # "The task is to ..."
    " it": 0.22,
    " then": 0.19,
    " in": 0.15,
    " on": 0.15,
    " at": 0.15,
    " no": 0.12,
    " this": 0.12,
    " when": 0.10,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    cur = tokens[-1]
    prev = tokens[-2] if len(tokens) > 1 else ""
    prev2 = tokens[-3] if len(tokens) > 2 else ""
    if len(tokens) == 1:  # a row's first token: " for" there is a strong trigger
        return None, 0.5 if cur == " for" else 0.0

    if cur == " with" and prev == " do" and prev2 == " to":

    if cur == " to" and prev == " due":
